substudy: Route2 Substudy 2 - Aggregation-Sensitive Compatibility Stability Check

claims.evidence_summary: Agreement distribution and divergence structure remained 2 full, 8 partial, 2 strong-divergence under local perturbation.
claims.interpretation_note: Aggregation remains the first major decision seam in this bounded Route 2 scope.

claims.evidence_summary: Worst-case still assigns coarse merge-caution labels to routing-facing cases that distributional separates.
claims.interpretation_note: Worst-case collapse behavior is robust under nearby panel substitutions.

claims.evidence_summary: Distributional still exposes confusable/needs_disambiguation/separable structure, including the perturbed moderate routing case.
claims.interpretation_note: Distributional gradation remains clear, but exact tier thresholds are still panel-dependent.

claims.evidence_summary: QA-blocked and mixed-QA triage cases continue to override structurally positive outcomes under QA-dominant aggregation.
claims.interpretation_note: QA-dominant remains a distinct operational family, not a weaker structural lens.

claims.evidence_summary: The perturbed panel remains interpretable with the same compact pattern set and predictor logic (QA regime + task relation).
claims.interpretation_note: Taxonomy viability survives this perturbation but should remain guarded as single-perturbation evidence.

claims.evidence_summary: Both aggregation-invariant and aggregation-sensitive case types remain present (2 invariant, 10 sensitive).
claims.interpretation_note: The invariant-versus-sensitive split remains interpretable and reusable.

claims.evidence_summary: Operational guidance remains unchanged: scenario-appropriate aggregation families produce better decision-relevant outputs.
claims.interpretation_note: Aggregation should continue to be treated as a workflow design variable in Route 2.
